_comment: Street RBA calls (economists and strategists). Update when an institution changes its view. For each bank: next_meeting = the RBA decision date the call refers to; call = hike | no change | cut; next_change = {month: YYYY-MM, optional label for approximate timing e.g. 'Mid 2027', direction: hike | cut, size_bp, rate_after}; as_of = date of the source; sources = links, newest first (the call bubble on the page links to sources[0], so put the article the current call comes from first). Set call to null if the bank has not published a view for the next meeting.

banks.note: Ashwin Clarke (CommBank, ABC 18 Nov, after Q3 wages): data 'reinforces our view that the RBA will be on edge', with 'some data to go to the December meeting'; expects growth to slow enough 'to stay the RBA's hand in H1 2027', 'allowing them to remain on hold before cutting rates twice in late 2027'. Belinda Allen (17 Nov): 'We judge December will not be a live meeting'; February remains live. Cuts pencilled in for August and November 2027

Luci Ellis (Westpac, 13 Nov, 'An RBA peak of greater conviction'): Bullock's 'take stock' comment read as 'a signal that the MPB would pause at the December meeting'; 'A rate hike in February 2027 cannot be ruled out but it is looking even less likely'; Westpac already 'believed the RBA cash rate was likely at a peak'. November Market Outlook has 'a move to cuts pencilled in for the second half of 2027'; cuts seen from August 2027 (Canstar, 3 Nov)

Sally Auld (NAB, 9 Nov): 'We think the RBA are done', with the RBA having signalled it could pause, though another increase isn't impossible with inflation the key risk. Earlier (Broker Daily, 4 Nov): 'we are not forecasting further policy tightening from here'; cuts seen from August 2027 (Canstar, 3 Nov)

ANZ (Grafa citing Capital Brief, 17 Nov, after RBA minutes): ANZ says the cash rate has peaked at 4.85%; Adam Boyton expects it to stay there 'for some time', with ANZ Research forecasting no change until the end of 2027, though a further rise 'cannot be entirely ruled out'. Cuts seen from November 2027 (Canstar, 3 Nov)

Shane Oliver (13 Nov): RBA 'has likely now done enough to slow demand which will cool inflation', with softer data bringing 'a reduced risk of further RBA rate hikes' (though market hike odds 'may be a bit too low'); 'rates will be on hold ahead of rate cuts late next year' and no cut 'until second half next year' absent a crisis. Earlier (6 Nov): RBA 'will pause in December'. Month and 25bp cut size assumed

George Tharenou (investingLive, 13 Nov): central case is an extended hold with policy restrictive through much of 2027 and no cuts until 'late 2027 or 2028', as 'the AI boom is giving Australia the inflation now and the productivity later'; February flagged as a possible hike if inflation surprises to the upside, and a near-term move is more likely a hike than a cut. November cut timing from UBS's earlier view; size assumed 25bp

Goldman Sachs (Grafa citing Capital Brief, 17 Nov, after RBA minutes): says the cash rate has peaked at 4.85% and the minutes were broadly consistent with the post-meeting press conference. December hold inferred from the peak call; no published timing for its next change

Tim Hext (19 Nov): no explicit December call; 'The Reserve Bank is achieving much earlier than expected what it set out to do with the five rate hikes this year' and 'will be cautious until inflation starts turning'; notes markets price a full cut by August 2027 and 'If rate cuts begin next year the cycle will be deeper than just two cuts'. No own timing published. Earlier, Steve Campbell (3 Nov): 'Further tightening can't be ruled out'
